newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn mulling 10 bln dmk rise in 97 borrowing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn mulling 10 bln dmk rise in 97 borrowing - paper.

text.p: The German government plans to expand its net borrowing by 10 billion marks in 1997 provided that the Bundesbank's gold and dollar reserves can be revalued this year, Berliner Morgenpost newspaper reported on Monday.
The newspaper said, citing unnamed senior sources within the coalition, that such a move would defuse a dispute about tax increases which has caused a rift within the coalition.

A spokeswoman for the Finance Ministry said in response to a Reuters enquiry that no decision had been taken on whether to increase net borrowing and that it was wrong to make the link between the revaluation of reserves and borrowing.
The spokeswoman also noted that Finance Minister Theo Waigel had made clear that a revaluation would only be used to retire old debt and not to narrow the budget deficit.
The newspaper said there was basically no disagreement between the government and the Bundesbank about the revaluation of reserves.

It said the bank itself had proposed the move at the start of the year because the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner to the European Central Bank (ECB), was urging central banks to harmonise the valuation of their reserves ahead of planned monetary union.
But it added the Bundesbank had problems with the timing of the revaluation since the central bank's annual profit is usually not distributed to Bonn until April of the following year.
The paper said the government was considering requesting that the Bundesbank set up an interim balance sheet to allow the revaluation to have an impact on Bonn's 1997 accounts.
The Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in the coalition government, piled pressure on Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Monday by insisting they will not let the 1998 budget include tax increases.
